title: Two finite cohomological inductions for an exact bifunctor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with derived categories and their standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category, $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$ a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], and $B:D(\mathcal A)\times D(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal T$ a bifunctor exact in each variable (preserving shifts and distinguished triangles in that variable). Let $\mathcal A_0,\mathcal B_0$ be classes of objects. Assume $B(F[0],G[0])\in\mathcal S$ for all $F\in\mathcal A_0,G\in\mathcal B_0$. Then $B(K,M)\in\mathcal S$ for all bounded $K,M$ with $H^q(K)\in\mathcal A_0$ and $H^q(M)\in\mathcal B_0$ for every $q$ for which the respective cohomology is nonzero. The zero objects and arbitrary finite cohomological intervals are included.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), applied successively in each variable

proof.text: An exact functor is additive [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For either fixed variable, its value on zero is zero: $1_{F(0)}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$, which characterizes a zero object in an additive category. Thus $B(0,M)$ and $B(K,0)$ lie in $\mathcal S$. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] and strict fullness, membership in $\mathcal S$ is preserved by isomorphisms and all integer shifts, and the middle vertex of a distinguished triangle belongs to $\mathcal S$ whenever its outer vertices do.

For any $L\in D(\mathcal C)$, where $\mathcal C$ is either given abelian category, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends] gives $H^r(\tau_{\le q}L)=H^r(L)$ for $r\le q$ and zero otherwise. If the cohomology of $L$ vanishes outside $[a,b]$, then $\tau_{\le a-1}L\simeq0$ and the canonical map $\tau_{\le b}L\to L$ is an isomorphism: on representatives the map $0\to\tau_{\le a-1}L$ and the latter inclusion are quasi-isomorphisms, hence are inverted in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The same argument shows that an acyclic $L$ is zero in its derived category.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; canonical-truncation cohomology calculation

proof.text: For every integer $q$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] supplies the distinguished triangle $$\tau_{\le q-1}L\longrightarrow\tau_{\le q}L\longrightarrow H^q(L)[-q]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le q-1}L)[1].$$ Applying $B$ with the other variable fixed gives a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal T$, with the final shift identified by exactness [def-weil-triangulated-category]. We use these triangles twice; no infinite tower or coproduct is taken.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, second displayed triangle with a=q-1; Tag 014V, definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories

proof.text: Fix $F\in\mathcal A_0$ and bounded $M$ as in the statement. Choose $c\le d$ containing its cohomological support. Induct on $j=0,\ldots,d-c+1$ to prove $B(F[0],\tau_{\le c-1+j}M)\in\mathcal S$. At $j=0$ this follows from steps 1 and 2. For a successor put $q=c+j$, with $0\le j\le d-c$, and apply $B(F[0],-)$ to the triangle of step 3. Its first vertex is in $\mathcal S$ by induction. If $H^q(M)=0$, its third vertex is zero. Otherwise $H^q(M)\in\mathcal B_0$, and $$B(F[0],H^q(M)[-q])\simeq B(F[0],H^q(M)[0])[-q]\in\mathcal S$$ by the hypothesis and shift closure. Thus its middle vertex is in $\mathcal S$ by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. At the last index $\tau_{\le d}M\simeq M$ by step 2. This proves $B(F[0],M)\in\mathcal S$ for every $F\in\mathcal A_0$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, finite induction in the second variable; Tag 05QM, definition-triangulated-subcategory

proof.text: Fix such an $M$ and bounded $K$ with cohomological support in $[a,b]$, $a\le b$. Induct on $j=0,\ldots,b-a+1$ to prove $B(\tau_{\le a-1+j}K,M)\in\mathcal S$. The initial term is zero by steps 1 and 2. For a successor set $q=a+j$, with $0\le j\le b-a$, and apply $B(-,M)$ to the triangle of step 3. Its first vertex is in $\mathcal S$ by induction. Its third vertex is zero if $H^q(K)=0$; otherwise $H^q(K)\in\mathcal A_0$ and step 4 followed by a shift gives $$B(H^q(K)[-q],M)\simeq B(H^q(K)[0],M)[-q]\in\mathcal S.$$ Extension closure [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] gives the middle vertex. The final term is isomorphic to $B(K,M)$ by step 2. Both intervals may start at any integer; gaps use the zero cases, without requiring zero to belong to either class. In particular this covers acyclic $K$ or $M$ and even empty classes.
